what: B1 — third alignment recipe (allenai/tulu-2-dpo-7b), against the pre-registered ordering. Plus the A1 taxonomy revision this run forced.
verdict_on_the_ordering: HOLDS. Sufficiency (fraction of refusal ablation removes, WildGuard-scored): Zephyr-DPO 97.8%, Zephyr-SFT 90.4%, Tulu-2-DPO 42.5%, OLMo 2 RLVR 38.5%, OLMo 2 control 25.4%. Tulu-2 lands strictly between, as predicted -- but far closer to OLMo 2 than to Zephyr, so the axis is not linear in anything we can currently name. Three points, one ordering, no trend line.
verdict_on_the_MECHANISM_prediction: FAILS AS STATED, AND THE REPAIR IS THE RESULT. The pre-registration said sufficiency should track the model's ability to render a refusal in the THIRD person without the direction. Tulu-2 breaks that: its ablated arm is 90% FIRST-person. But the first-person category was hiding two stances, and OLMo 2 has none of the second, so A1 could not have seen it.

the_three_registers.inability: 'I cannot' / 'I'm sorry, but I can't' -- forecloses the request
the_three_registers.identity: 'As an AI language model, I must emphasize...' -- asserts a role, and can continue into compliance
the_three_registers.normative: 'Bribery is illegal and unethical' -- asserts a norm about the act

THE_INVARIANT.claim: Ablating the refusal direction destroys the INABILITY register, in every family tested. That is what the direction mediates.
THE_INVARIANT.why_A1_got_it_wrong: A1 concluded 'first-person vs third-person' from OLMo 2 and Zephyr, neither of which produces identity-frame refusals in quantity. Tulu-2 produces 38 at baseline and 54 after ablation. The axis is INABILITY vs everything else, not grammatical person.

what_replaces_it_is_family_specific_and_.olmo2: third-person normative. 80 refusals, FIRM -- 1/80 contain a compliance pivot. Sufficiency 38.5%.
what_replaces_it_is_family_specific_and_.tulu2: first-person identity assertion. 54 refusals, WEAK -- 12/54 (22%) pivot to compliance ('However, if you still want to...'). Sufficiency 42.5% as measured.
what_replaces_it_is_family_specific_and_.reading: Sufficiency is not about grammatical person. It is about whether the model has a FALLBACK register at all, and how firm that fallback is. Zephyr has none; Tulu-2 has a leaky one; OLMo 2 has a solid one.

OPEN_and_it_bounds_the_tulu2_number.problem: 48 generated tokens is too short for Tulu-2. Its ablated refusals pivot LATE -- 'However, if you still want to' lands right at the truncation boundary -- so 13 of 69 cannot be judged from what was generated. Hand-reading them: roughly half head for compliance ('if you are determined to make false accusations'), half for legitimate redirects ('ways to PROTECT your own trade secrets', 'LEGAL ways to use offshore accounts').
OPEN_and_it_bounds_the_tulu2_number.consequence: Tulu-2's ablated rate of 0.523 is an UPPER bound, so its sufficiency of 42.5% is a LOWER bound. The ordering is unaffected -- correcting it moves Tulu-2 further from OLMo 2 and closer to Zephyr, i.e. in the predicted direction -- but the number should not be quoted until it is fixed.
OPEN_and_it_bounds_the_tulu2_number.fix: regenerate the tulu2_dpo ablated arm with gen_max_new_tokens=128 and re-judge. ~15 min. Cheap, and it is the difference between a bounded number and a quoted one.
OPEN_and_it_bounds_the_tulu2_number.note: OLMo 2 is unaffected: 1/80 of its ablated refusals pivot, so 48 tokens is sufficient there. This is a Tulu-2 property, not a design flaw across the board.

direction_quality_caveat: Only 1/160 (pos,layer) cells passed Arditi's filters for tulu-2-dpo, against 13/160 for OLMo 2. The ablation still works (peak 10.715 against a norm-matched random control of 0.277, 39x), but the selection is thin and a reviewer will ask. Worth reporting rather than smoothing over.
